episodes.193948: A strong to severe thunderstorm developed during the evening hours over southern Lincoln County. The storm produced damaging winds in the Flintville area.
episodes.193976: A well-defined cold front associated with a strong upper level low produced widespread wind damage in western Wisconsin, as well as three tornadoes in Pierce and St Croix Counties on August 29th, 2024.
episodes.193985: On the evening of August 28th, a line of strong thunderstorms pushed northwestward across Apalachee Bay and made landfall across portions of coastal Wakulla and coastal Franklin counties with measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.  A similar pattern occurred again during the evening of August 29th.
episodes.194016: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and several areas of flash flooding across Eastern NC.
episodes.194017: Isolated to scattered strong thunderstorms developed in southern middle Tennessee in the afternoon. A few of them produced some damaging winds.
episodes.194026: Abundant monsoonal moisture continued to be pulled northward into New Mexico on August 28th and 29th. This resulted in showers and thunderstorms producing locally heavy rainfall developing over the recent burn scars by Ruidoso. The first round on August 28th resulted in flash flooding within the Cherokee Mobile Home Park down from the Salt burn scar, and within and near the South Fork burn scar. The second round on August 29th resulted in flash flooding from the South Fork and McBride burn scars. Thunderstorms producing heavy rain resulting in flash flooding also impacted parts of Portales, NM on August 29th.
episodes.194031: Isolated thunderstorms developed across the southern South Plains on the afternoon of the 30th. A very moist atmosphere was able to generate efficient rain producing thunderstorms. A slow moving isolated thunderstorm moving across southern Lynn County produced a wet microburst. Areas along US Highway 87 between O'Donnell and Tahoka were reported to have approximately six inches of water flowing over the roadway. Crop damage from wind-driven hail and roof damage to a barn were also reported.
episodes.194038: As a ridge of high pressure that had been centered over the central Mississippi River Valley shifted eastward toward the Southeast U.S. coastline, southerly to southeasterly flow brought sufficient moisture advection to spark the return of scattered thunderstorms across Central Alabama by August 28. High DCAPE values, in some instances over 1200-1300 J/kg, aided in downburst activity for several consecutive afternoons. Most impacted were the cities of Mountain Brook and Alexander City, both on August 29, where scattered to widespread tree and power line damage occurred. Several homes and a couple businesses sustained heavy damage in Alexander City as well.
episodes.194039: Thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee on August 29, 2024. While these were non-severe, they did produce gusty winds. One particular thunderstorm in Williamson County snapped a few trees near College Grove.
episodes.194043: More summertime thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours of August 30, 2024. Gusty winds were the primary threat with these thunderstorms, and one particular storm in Manchester snapped a tree onto a powerline. Elsewhere, a man in Crossville was severely injured after being struck by lightning.
episodes.194061: Numerous thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon of August 30th. Due to a modest instability - low wind shear environment, these thunderstorms were pulse in nature with wet microbursts being the primary threat. Although an abundance of microbursts occurred, only one was severe in Missouri, producing minor wind damage.
episodes.194062: Numerous thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front during the afternoon of August 30th. Due to a modest instability - low wind shear environment, these thunderstorms were pulse in nature with wet microbursts being the primary threat. Although an abundance of microbursts occurred, only one was severe in Macoupin, producing tree damage. A landspout also developed along outflow passing through Randolph County, producing minor damage along its path.
episodes.194128: A cold front moved into Eastern North Carolina from the north during the afternoon of August 30th. Out ahead of this front, the seabreeze combined with multiple boundaries leftover from the prior days thunderstorm activity to provide a focus for additional shower and thunderstorm development during the afternoon on August 30th. A few of these storms became strong to severe in nature, mainly across the Pamlico Sound bringing a threat for waterspouts in the strongest storms.
episodes.194197: Heavy rainfall along a stalled boundary led to instances of flash flooding.
episodes.194198: Heavy rainfall along a stalled boundary led to instances of flash flooding.
episodes.194217: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours, and dissipated shortly after sunset. A couple of the thunderstorms were strong to severe. One storm knocked down power lines and leaned power poles in northern Madison County, resulting a power outage of about 700 residents.
episodes.194259: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm and humid airmass.
episodes.194260: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm and humid airmass.
episodes.194355: Hot and humid day with increasing upper level heights kept the area largely dry, however, isolated convection was able to kick off  along a few old outflow boundaries from the previous day, with just enough dry air aloft to potentially see damaging wind gusts with stronger updrafts.
episodes.194736: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts at Cape Canaveral and in St Lucie County.
episodes.194737: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard and St Lucie County coasts.
episodes.195372: A couple of thunderstorms produced gale-force winds over the middle tidal Potomac River.
episodes.195466: An upper level centered over Texas began driving moisture into the local area a couple days prior to this event. By the 30th, the atmospheric moisture content had reached values near the record for this time of year. Storms that developed in this environment were able to tap into this moisture to produce quite heavy rainfall and when combined with slow storm movement, produced flash flooding over New Orleans.
episodes.195514: A frontal boundary moving south from east-central Virginia into central North Carolina combined with a disturbance aloft and produced numerous showers and storms in the afternoon to late evening hours. Storms initially formed over the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain, congealing and tracking west-southwestward in the evening hours over the western and southern Piedmont and Sandhills. Numerous downed trees and power lines resulted, as well as flash flooding.
episodes.195580: A severe thunderstorm developed over southern St. Clair County.
episodes.195787: Strong surface heating produced unstable conditions across the Mid-South by the mid-afternoon on August 30, 2024. Numerous thunderstorms developed across north Mississippi and West Tennessee. A few storms were severe with damaging winds.
episodes.195788: Strong surface heating produced unstable conditions across the Mid-South by the mid-afternoon on August 30, 2024. Numerous thunderstorms developed across north Mississippi and West Tennessee. A few storms were severe with damaging winds.
episodes.195794: On the afternoon and evening of August 29th, 2024, a surface cold front was entering western Kansas from the northwest.  Ahead of the southward moving boundary was an area of enhanced moisture convergence as a weal surface trough was in place over western Kansas and southeast Colorado.  This area would prove to be the impetus for rapidly developing mid-afternoon thunderstorms that produces numerous 55 mph wind gusts and higher; the highest of which was measured at 74 mph just east of Garden City. Damage to a section of roof was noted at the Meade High School.
episodes.195865: As diurnal heating increased and the Atlantic sea breeze focused over Southwest Florida, this provided sufficient instability for several thunderstorms across the region and local Gulf waters in the afternoon of August 30th.
episodes.195871: Scattered thunderstorms developed over the North Carolina mountains during the early afternoon and moved out over the foothills during mid-afternoon. A few of the storms produced strong-to-damaging wind gusts and hail.
episodes.195872: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon into the evening. A few of the storms produced brief strong-to-damaging wind gusts. In addition, the storms tended to move slowly, and one slow-moving storm cluster produced very heavy rainfall and flash flooding in York County.
episodes.195902: A few isolated diurnally driven thunderstorms developed the afternoon of the 29th. Some 1 to 1.25 inch hail was reported in the northern ATL metro, otherwise impacts were localized wind damage.
episodes.195903: A few strong afternoon thunderstorms were able to develop the afternoon of the 30th. Impacts were mostly wind based, however a few hail reports were also noted.
episodes.195906: During the late afternoon of the 30th, a developing line of strong to severe thunderstorms impacted far southern portions of the Chicago WFO CWA producing a few instances of hail and wind damage.
episodes.195907: During the late afternoon of the 30th, a developing line of strong to severe thunderstorms impacted far southern portions of the Chicago WFO CWA producing a few instances of hail and wind damage.
episodes.195926: A strong cold front was centered over the region and was the trigger for several showers and storms. Some of these storms produced damaging winds which brought down many trees. Lightning from one thunderstorm struck a tree, which caught on fire, in Campbell county.
episodes.195952: The cold front that was over the region on the 29th, made limited progress eastward on the 30th. This feature continued to serve as the focus for afternoon and evening shower and thunderstorm development. A few of these storms increased to severe levels causing damaging winds which downed trees.  The storms were noted to have produced heavy downpours due to high rainfall rates, at times reaching 3 to 4 inches per hour which caused localized flash flooding in Ashe County.
episodes.195960: The cold front that was over the region on the 29th, made limited progress eastward on the 30th. This feature continued to serve as the focus for afternoon and evening shower and thunderstorm development. A few of these storms increased to severe levels causing damaging winds which downed trees. There were also two occurrence of hail ranging from nickel to quarter size.
episodes.196039: There was an isolated report of one inch diameter hail in Kalamazoo county on August 30th.
episodes.196042: A cold front interacting with a seasonably warm and moist environment triggered clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms across central Illinois during the afternoon and evening of August 30th.  One cell dropped nickel-sized hail, while others produced wind gusts of around 60mph and minor wind damage.  In addition, urban flash flooding occurred across portions of Springfield and Champaign.  No road closures or water rescues were reported.
episodes.196045: During the late afternoon and evening hours on August 29th, storms of various modes moved across portions of northeast Iowa bringing strong winds causing several instances of tree and structural damage.
episodes.196047: During the late afternoon and evening hours on August 29th, storms of various modes moved across portions of southeast Minnesota bringing isolated wind damage. Additionally, the heavy rainfall from storms caused urban flooding in Winona which resulted in numerous streets being flooded and one instance of a vehicle being inundated with water.
episodes.196048: During the late afternoon and evening hours on August 29th, storms of various modes produced isolated tree damage in Buffalo County.
episodes.196193: Scattered thunderstorms developed and trained along a stationary front draped across central Virginia on the night of August 29. These storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding given slow storm motions and cell mergers. Damaging wind gusts also occurred with the strongest storms.
episodes.196194: Scattered thunderstorms developed and trained along a stationary front draped across central Virginia on the night of August 29. These storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding given slow storm motions and cell mergers. Damaging wind gusts also occurred with the strongest storms.
episodes.196242: Scattered showers and thunderstorms reached a maximum in coverage over the Florida Keys coastal waters embedded in freshening east to southeast lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.196356: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a waterspout over West Central Florida waters and strong marine wind gusts across the Nature Coast waters.
episodes.196357: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze cause a residential fire due to lightning in Pinellas County.
episodes.200451: At the surface, an occluded low drifted northeastward across far-northwestern ON and Hudson Bay during the late afternoon of August 30th through the first couple predawn hours of the 31st. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front drifted eastward across the OH/PA border region and toward central portions of NY and PA, while the trailing cold front moved eastward from the southwestern Great Lakes and Lower MO Valley to north-central OH and the Lower to Mid OH Valley. Within the warm and moist sector between these two fronts, isolated to scattered multicell thunderstorms developed in northern OH and produced isolated straight-line convective wind damage amidst weak to moderate MUCAPE, moderate to strong DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear during the late afternoon through late evening.
